## Paper Overview

The paper "Self-Consuming Generative Models Go MAD" was presented at the 12th International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024) in Vienna, Austria.

## Authors

The authors are Sina Alemohammad, Josue Casco-Rodriguez, Lorenzo Luzi, Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun, Hossein Babaei, Daniel LeJeune, Ali Siahkoohi, and Richard G. Baraniuk.

## Main Research Focus

The paper examines how advances in generative AI algorithms have led to using AI-synthesized data to train next-generation models, and how repeating this process creates an autophagous ("self-consuming") loop whose properties are poorly understood.

## Key Findings

The primary conclusion is that without enough fresh real data in each generation of an autophagous loop, future generative models are doomed to have their quality (precision) or diversity (recall) progressively decrease. This condition is termed Model Autophagy Disorder (MAD), by analogy to mad cow disease.

The research demonstrates that appreciable MADness can occur in only a handful of generations.

## Methodology

The researchers conducted a thorough analytical and empirical analysis using state-of-the-art generative image models of three families of autophagous loops that differ in how fixed or fresh real training data is available through the generations of training and whether the samples from previous-generation models have been biased to trade off data quality versus diversity.

   import numpy as np

   for each feature:
       gen1 = data[depth==1][feature]
       gen2p = data[depth>=2][feature]
       
       # pooled SD
       n1, n2 = len(gen1), len(gen2p)
       pooled_sd = np.sqrt(((n1-1)*gen1.std()**2 + (n2-1)*gen2p.std()**2) / (n1+n2-2))
       
       # equivalence bound in raw units
       delta = d_bound * pooled_sd

       se = pooled_sd * np.sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2)

"""TOST equivalence test: gen-1 vs gen-2+ for all 7 features."""
import json, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

data_path = "/root/gen-depth-fingerprint/data/features_8gen.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_path)

depth_col = 'depth' if 'depth' in df.columns else 'generation'
print(f"Depth column: {depth_col}")
print(f"Value counts:\n{df[depth_col].value_counts().sort_index()}")

gen1 = df[df[depth_col] == 1]
gen2p = df[df[depth_col] >= 2]
print(f"gen-1: {len(gen1)}, gen-2+: {len(gen2p)}")

features = {
    'entropy_mean': 'drifting',
    'entropy_std': 'intermediate',
    'entropy_max': 'near-stationary',
    'entropy_min': 'intermediate',
    'tail_decay': 'near-stationary',
    'ttr': 'drifting',
    'hapax_ratio': 'drifting',
}

d_bound = 0.20  # Cohen's d equivalence threshold (small effect)
results = {"equivalence_bound_d": d_bound, "alpha": 0.05, "features": {}}

print(f"\n{'Feature':20s} | {'Group':16s} | {'d':>8s} | {'p_TOST':>12s} | Result")
print("-" * 80)

for feat, group in features.items():
    col = feat
    if col not in df.columns:
        for v in [feat, feat.replace('_', ''), feat.replace('_', '-')]:
            if v in df.columns:
                col = v
                break
        else:
            print(f"{feat:20s} | COLUMN NOT FOUND, skipping")

    s1, s2 = x1.std(ddof=1), x2.std(ddof=1)

    delta = d_bound * pooled_sd
    diff = x1.mean() - x2.mean()
    se = pooled_sd * np.sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2)
    dof = n1 + n2 - 2
    cohens_d = diff / pooled_sd

    t_lower = (diff + delta) / se
    p_lower = 1 - stats.t.cdf(t_lower, dof)

    t_upper = (diff - delta) / se
    p_upper = stats.t.cdf(t_upper, dof)

    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)
    equivalent = bool(p_tost < 0.05)

    results["features"][feat] = {
        "group": group,
        "n_gen1": int(n1), "n_gen2p": int(n2),
        "mean_gen1": round(float(x1.mean()), 6),
        "mean_gen2p": round(float(x2.mean()), 6),
        "mean_diff": round(float(diff), 6),
        "pooled_sd": round(float(pooled_sd), 6),
        "observed_d": round(float(cohens_d), 4),
        "delta_raw": round(float(delta), 6),
        "t_lower": round(float(t_lower), 4),
        "p_lower": float(p_lower),
        "t_upper": round(float(t_upper), 4),
        "p_upper": float(p_upper),
        "p_tost": float(p_tost),
        "equivalent_at_alpha_005": equivalent
    }

    print(f"{feat:20s} | {group:16s} | {cohens_d:+8.4f} | {p_tost:12.2e} | {tag}")

out_path = "/root/gen-depth-fingerprint/results/tost_equivalence.json"
